sources.title: President of India · Ol Chiki centenary, 16 February 2026
sources.note: President’s Secretariat release dated 16 February 2026. It attributes the script’s creation to Raghunath Murmu in 1925 and names earlier writing systems. The commemoration date is separate from the attributed origin date; this is an institutional account, not a manuscript study.

sources.title: Unicode 17.0 · Ol Chiki, section 13.10.1
sources.note: The Structure and Modifier Letters passages describe left-to-right writing, standalone vowel letters, nasalization, vowel length and the baseline vowel modifier. Used for writing-system structure, not current speaker numbers or a pronunciation lesson.

sources.title: Sahitya Akademi · Santali award register
sources.note: The official Santali table lists Nalha, poetry, Gobinda Chandra Majhi, 2016. This is an award record; the poems and a particular edition have not been reviewed here.

sources.title: Sahitya Akademi · Annual report 2022–2023
sources.note: PDF page 145, printed page 144: the 21 May 2022 Baripada symposium, Damayanti Beshra’s role and regional presentations. Selected account inspected in the original report. It records a past event, not a current visiting opportunity.

sources.title: Santali trilingual learning booklet · first edition, November 2018
sources.note: Selected credits and table pages (PDF pages 3 and 10) inspected on 1 October 2026; fresh retrieval failed on 21 October. No fluent-speaker review of vocabulary or pronunciation; pages are not reproduced.

sources.title: C-16: Population by mother tongue, Odisha — 2011
sources.note: Original C-16 workbook, Sheet1, row 116: individual Santali entry 018040, 859,947 people in Odisha. District counts use that same entry. These are reported mother tongues in 2011, not current speaker or ethnic-community totals; no script-use measure is supplied.
